question.text: Which of the following best describes the regulatory framework for issuance of ADRs/GDRs (Depository Receipts) by Indian companies in international markets?

answer.text: The issuing company must comply with the listing requirements of the chosen foreign stock exchange and applicable exchange-control/foreign-holding regulations
Any company registered in India can issue ADRs/GDRs without any restrictions
Only government-owned companies can issue ADRs/GDRs
Only companies listed on BSE can issue ADRs/GDRs

explanation.text: The Logic: Depository Receipts are shares of a local company that are listed outside India (Series XII workbook pages 56-57). The issuing company must comply with the listing requirements of the foreign stock exchange where the DRs are to be listed and with the applicable exchange-control regulations governing foreign holding (page 85). The Trap: Not every Indian company can freely issue ADRs/GDRs — eligibility depends on the rules of the foreign exchange concerned and on Indian exchange-control rules. The requirement is not limited to government-owned or BSE-listed companies. Note: ADRs/GDRs allow Indian companies to raise capital from international investors by listing depository receipts representing their shares on foreign stock exchanges.
